speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and when exactly it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance with bright red cheeks, and does the body rash look lacy or net-like? I also need to confirm if she has had any recent contact with other children who have similar symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash that spares the perioral area followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
